Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Anurag Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 420 of 2022, under sections 41, 411 & 413 I.P.C., Police Station Taryasujan, District Kushinagar.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant was not arrested from the spot but his name was mentioned in the F.I.R. on the basis of confessional statement of co-accused persons.
It is also submitted that nothing was recovered from the door of the applicant the said vehicles were being scrapped by co-accused persons those are residents of the same village.

There is no any criminal history against the applicant and there is no evidence on record to show the complicity of the present applicant, if any, scrapping the vehicles with other co-accused persons.

It Dharmendra Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97576162/
1 is also submitted that other co-accused persons had already been granted anticipatory bail by the learned court of Session by order dated 07.11.2022 and on the similar facts the bail application of present applicant was refused.

sentences.text: Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Dharmendra Chauhan, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make him available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
